feeds.title: Map of the Week
feeds.description: Map of the Week is a Cartographer/GIS/map nut by trade originally from Philadelphia now living in exile outside of Boston, Mass.

feeds.title: The Map Room Blog
feeds.description: The Map Room is a blog about maps by Jonathan Crowe that covers everything from antique map collecting to the latest in geospatial technology.

feeds.title: SomethingAboutMaps
feeds.description: Hi I'm Daniel Huffman, and I am a cartographer. I have always loved maps, and would sometimes go to the library and browse atlases for fun. I make maps, and occasionally teach about cartography, in Madison, WI.

feeds.title: International Cartographic Association
feeds.description: The International Cartographic Association (ICA) promotes the discipline and profession of Cartography and GIScience in an international context. Find posts and updates on GIScience and Cartography.

feeds.title: Avenza Systems Inc. Blog
feeds.description: Avenza is the producer of the popular MAPublisher and Geographic Imager mapping and spatial imaging solutions for Adobe Creative Cloud as well as the new and innovative Avenza Maps app and digital map store solution for iOS, Android, and Windows devices. MAPublisher provides over 50 precision cartographic and GIS tools that map-makers need.

feeds.title: OCAD Blog
feeds.description: OCAD is a drawing program created for the needs of the cartographer. This focus in cartography makes it extremely easy and convenient to use. OCAD has all the capabilities to create any kind of maps.

feeds.title: DETROITography
feeds.description: Featuring and creating great maps of Detroit! We encourage others to make their own maps of Detroit too. Share yours with us and get featured!

feeds.title: Lovell Johns Blog
feeds.description: Lovell Johns is a cartographic and GIS company founded in 1965. Lovell Johns is a leading UK mapping company providing GIS and other map services to the public sector, publishers and all sizes of business.Keep up to date with the Lovell Johns blog to find out the latest news from the mapping Industry.

feeds.title: ART & CARTOGRAPHY
feeds.description: ART & CARTOGRAPHY is maintained by the Commission on Art & Cartography of the International Cartographic Association (ICA). We explore the increasing relations between art and cartography, and to stimulate new forms of interaction. The goal is to provide an environment in which artists, researchers, architects, cartographers and citizen in general can have access to different sources.

feeds.title: Mapping as Process
feeds.description: Dive into Cartopgraphy insights in Mapping as Process - a blog on the study of mapping processes, on the production, circulation, and consumption of maps, to delineate mapping discourses and modes. Explore a myriad of musings and discerning patterns in historical data that can be used to reveal insights into mapping processes.

feeds.title: Adventures In Mapping
feeds.description: Adventures In Mapping illuminates the art and science of Cartoprahy further by sharing thoughtful ideas and stories from the history of Map-making. The author also shares strategies, recreations, guides on what tools to use, and their personal favorite reimagined maps for readers to enjoy.

feeds.title: Big Think » Strange Maps
feeds.description: In an increasingly remote world, it's more important than ever that you have a scalable, digital resource to build culture and enable transformation. Unlock potential across your organization by building the capabilities that are relevant today and will continue to be relevant in the future with Big Think+.They have a section that focuses on Strange Maps, their cartography, geography, political division and feature stories with other related topics.

feeds.title: Stamen Blog
feeds.description: Enjoy musings on data visualization, map making, and everything else from Stamen Design. Stay in the loop of the latest Cartographic events taking place across the world. Stamen is a data visualization and cartography studio that helps people create novel and sophisticated data products.

feeds.title: David Rumsey Blog
feeds.description: David Rumsey's Blog features his collection which includes 18th and 19th-century historical North and South American atlases, globes, school geographies, maritime charts, and separate maps including wall, pocket, and manuscripts. Historic maps of the World, Europe, Asia, and Africa are also represented.

feeds.title: World Anvil Blog » Mapmaking
feeds.description: Explore the Mapmaking segment by World Anvil and access a treasure trove of map-making tips and insights tailored to help you create breath-taking worlds. World Anvil is an online toolset specifically designed for worldbuilding, perfect for authors, writers, game developers, and tabletop gamers.

feeds.title: Profantasy's Map-Making Journal
feeds.description: Dive into the latest offerings by ProFantasy in their blog journal. Browse through some of the wonderful maps created by the Profantasy user community. ProFantasy is an industry-standard map-making software for tabletop roleplaying and wargames.

feeds.title: Esri UK Blog
feeds.description: Esri UK is the world's leading provider of geographic information systems (GIS), creating technology that gives you access to maps, apps, and analytics. The people of Esri UK, share more about their work, inspiration, and how to get the most out of Esri UK technology on their blog.

feeds.title: Geography and Digital Cartography
feeds.description: The Geography and Cartography Blog' is a page about maps and spatial analysis. Moreover, our goal is to show relevant matters about World, notably Brazilian Amazon region through maps and graphics as well as inspire cartographers of the future to create amazing maps.

feeds.title: Fantasy Cartography » Youtube
feeds.description: Find videos on Cartography.

feeds.title: The Marauding Carto-nerd
feeds.description: Hi I'm Kenneth Field. Maps are my passion and my profession. This is my personal cartonerd blog where I offer opinions and critique maps. Find blogs about maps.

feeds.title: Guerrilla Cartography Blog
feeds.description: Guerrilla Cartography is a loose band of cartographers, researchers, and designers intent on widely promoting the cartographic arts and facilitating an expansion of the art, methods, and thematic scope of cartography.

feeds.title: Sound Cartography
feeds.description: Sound Cartography is a selection of sound maps over the world. Cartography of sound, Noise maps, Soundscapes, Sound recordings, etc.

feeds.title: Mapa Jeff Cartography
feeds.description: I came to mapping in my 30s after earlier jobs in travel publishing, technical editing, and journalism. I built my map technique from scratch over a dozen years - starting with pen drawings at a seaside café, and culminating in terabytes of computer files and an office full of gear. Find posts and updates on maps and cartography.

feeds.title: The Map Kiwi
feeds.description: Hi I'm Andrew Douglas-Clifford, and until recently I was a Masters in Geographic Information Science (MGIS) student at the University of Canterbury. I am passionate about maps, cartography and GIS, and enjoy creating maps as a hobby. Find posts and updates on maps and cartography.

feeds.title: Afternoon Map
feeds.description: The Afternoon Map is a member of MENAlab, a constellation of independent internet destinations focused on the history, society, and culture. Find cartography blogs dedicated to presenting quality maps with a maximum pixel-to-word ratio, brought to you by Ottoman History Podcast

feeds.title: ICA Commission on Planetary Cartography
feeds.description: The International Cartographic Association (ICA) Commission on Planetary Cartography was officially established as a continuation of the ICA Planetary Cartography Working Group at the ICA Congress in Ottawa in August 1999. We promote and document planetary cartographic products. We encourage cartographers, researchers, graphic artists, and students to join the planetary cartographic community.

feeds.title: The Wandering Cartographer
feeds.description: Before I became a cartographer, I spent ten years teaching wilderness travel at the National Outdoor Leadership School. I picked up GIS skills from a diamond exploration outfit in Canada's Northwest Territories As a cartographer I split his time between topographic trail maps and doing historical mapping.

feeds.title: Radical Cartography
feeds.description: Find posts and updates on Cartography.

feeds.title: A Cartographic View
feeds.description: Find posts and updates on Cartography.

feeds.title: Psychocartography
feeds.description: Psychocartography is a interpretation and representation of landscape, architecture and the urban environment in graphics, sound, film and text. I am a landscape architect with an interest in the role space, place, city and landscape have to play in defining the human condition- and vice versa. Find posts and updates on maps.

feeds.title: Cartoblography
feeds.description: Kenneth Field is an academic cartographer and geographer from the UK where he taught in UK Universities for 20 years. In his blog, Cartoblography, he intends to share musings on matters of mapping, share his recent work, and focus a spotlight on maps that interest him.

feeds.title: Mappenstance
feeds.description: Mappenstance compiles thoughts and observations on the rhetoric of cartography from students in the Department of Rhetoric & Communication Studies at the University of Richmond. Browse a well-curated collection of Vintage maps, Informative sources, and some amazing stories.

feeds.title: Atlas of Design
feeds.description: Follow the latest news and updates covering Atlas of Design. The Atlas of Design is a book dedicated to showing off some of the world's most beautiful and intriguing cartographic designs. Every two years, a new volume is published filled with full-color maps, selected from a worldwide competition, and judged by an expert panel.

feeds.title: MapChart Blog
feeds.description: MapChart's Blog shares new features, updates, behind-the-scenes, and tips on creating your custom maps. Established in 2014, Mapchart is an online platform providing users and map enthusiasts with all the tools and resources they require to build awesome maps.

feeds.title: The Map Shop » Cartography
feeds.description: Enjoy Cartography articles that delve into the art and science of map creation, providing users with a plethora of tools and resources to bring their geographical visions to life. The Map Shop is a passionate group of geographers, cartographers, designers, and travelers that provides Map-making resources to customers online.

feeds.title: Map Effects
feeds.description: Discover fantastic Fantasy Map-making ideas and guides from Map Effects in their blog. From simple Drawing tips to Complete Photoshop guides, you will find every Map-making essential here. Map Effects is a one-stop solution for fantasy map-making and provides all kinds of Map-building resources online.

feeds.title: British Cartographic Society Blog
feeds.description: Find all the latest news and information resources from the BCS via their blog. Stay up-to-date on what's happening in International Cartography circles. The British Cartographic Society is a charity registered in England and Wales that offers a unique forum for exchanging ideas and sharing knowledge on all aspects of maps and mapmaking.

feeds.title: Old Maps Library Blog
feeds.description: Old Maps Library, founded in 2015, sells beautiful reproductions of Maps and Illustrations from the 17th to early 19th centuries at London & Edinburgh Street Markets. Their blog takes readers on a journey through the eyes of historians and cartographers, and highlights how they've imprinted their dreams and drawn their ideas.

feeds.title: Cartography Room Blog
feeds.description: Embark on a worldwide mapping journey as the Author travels and explores a series of hidden, forgotten cities that once were places of importance. The Cartography Room Blog shares maps and images of postage stamps of lost places, history tidbits, and the author's thoughts and observations about why these places were lost.

feeds.title: GeoCurrents Blog » Cartography
feeds.description: Learn about remarkable global shifts across political and social spectrums through Cartography. GeoCurrents Blog is dedicated to exploring the geographical and historical patterns that underlie the world's current events and that structure global and regional relationships. Maps are used in all posts to show and illustrate the processes involved.

feeds.title: Cartographers' Guild
feeds.description: The Cartographers' Guild is a forum created by and for map makers and aficionados, a place where every aspect of cartography can be admired, examined, learned, and discussed. We love to share our maps, to help one another improve our maps, and to pool our mapping resources.

feeds.title: Gretchen N. Peterson
feeds.description: Cartographer's Toolkit is like a big cheat-sheet for cartography. Follow the blog, in which ideas ranging from best practices to design to the profession of cartography are explored. Authored by Gretchen Peterson whose first book, GIS Cartography, is a guidebook for the GIS professional, distilled from 10 years of experience as a GIS professional.

feeds.title: Geomaticblog
feeds.description: Find information on Geomatics, Cartography, Location and everything else.
